clue.text: Jetty about to slip into the water

indicators.note: the jetty word goes around the slip word, so it sits about it

parts.note: a jetty is a pier
to slip up is to err

explanation.surface: Someone on a jetty is about to tumble into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container. 'the water' is not the sea but a brand of French bottled mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Perrier is a well-known brand of sparkling mineral water from France.

clue.text: Quick pint after the concert?

indicators.note: the pint abbreviation is placed following the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms in London

explanation.surface: A suggestion of a speedy drink once the gig is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt and quick are synonyms describing something done without delay.

clue.text: Outcome for Ulster — fantastic!

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheer for a good result for the Northern Irish province.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the outcome of an event, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One who butts in may be Leo, printer extraordinary

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Leo, an exceptional printer, may be nosy and intrusive.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper is an intruder who meddles in the affairs of others.

clue.text: It's cold in space, I'd say!

indicators.note: the speaker pronouncing a word signals a sound-alike

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A remark on how chilly it is in outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the watery discharge from eyes and nose, the stuff of a head cold.

clue.text: Tea-time treat politician dropped in the salt?

indicators.note: the politician is put down inside the salt container

parts.note: a cruet holds salt at the table, so the salt suggests a cruet
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a politician fell into the salt at tea-time.
explanation.walkthrough: A CRUMPET is a British griddle cake eaten toasted with butter at tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumpets are a classic British afternoon tea snack, toasted and buttered.

clue.text: Vicar is honest, introducing rogues initially to exercises

indicators.note: the honest word takes in the other pieces, introducing them inside

parts.note: clean, as in a clean record, means honest

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of rogues

parts.note: gym is short for gymnastics, physical exercises

explanation.surface: An honest vicar brings rogues to his exercise classes to reform them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of 'rogues'; 'introducing' means the honest word is split open to take in that letter and the exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, one kind of clergyman.

clue.text: Surgeon dispatching boy on impulse

indicators.note: dispatching means sending away, so the boy's letters are removed

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A surgeon sends a boy off on a sudden whim.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong impulse or desire to do something.

clue.text: Artistic jumble — surprisingly it's cheap

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A remark that a jumbled artwork is oddly inexpensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is an artistic work imitating or mixing others' styles, a medley.

clue.text: Lament for the late railway, done up inside after the cut

indicators.note: the railway part follows the shortened word
a cut word loses its last letter, here the word the
the rearranged letters go inside the railway abbreviation
done up means redone or renovated, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A lament for a closed railway line, refurbished after the cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done up' rearranges the word done, and 'inside' puts it within the railway letters; 'cut' trims the last letter. 'for the late' completes the mourning picture: this is a song for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a song or poem of mourning, a lament for someone who has died.

clue.text: Filming the assault?

definitions.meaning: being filmed means being in front of the cameras at the studio
an attack or charge, as the first rush of a battle

explanation.surface: A question about shooting a battle scene for a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means an attack, while the two-word phrase means at the place where filming happens.

clue.text: Terribly green is the queen — this'll get things going!

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A remark that the queen looks awfully green, with a pick-me-up offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges only GREEN, into ENERG; IS stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An energiser is something that invigorates or starts things moving.

clue.text: Journey of quiet girl excited by picture

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: an image is a picture

explanation.surface: A quiet girl is thrilled by a photograph of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey, typically one made to a sacred place.

clue.text: Look! I go among the people

indicators.note: the single letter goes into the middle of the people word

parts.note: men means people, as in the men and women of a crowd

explanation.surface: An announcement of someone going out to mingle with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien means a person's appearance or look, especially as showing mood.

clue.text: Settling loans, I get spoken of as thick

parts.note: subs are advances or loans of money, especially against wages

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than spelt, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: dense means thick

explanation.surface: Someone settling up loans and being called stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsidence is the gradual settling or sinking of ground or a building.

clue.text: When playing up, one method is to look amazed

indicators.note: playing about with words signals their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach advises that when playing up, one should look astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges UP ONE METHOD; 'When' and 'is to look' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be open-mouthed is to gape in amazement or astonishment.

clue.text: Measure of French taste, not the first to try

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
de is French for of

indicators.note: the first letter of the taste word is dropped

parts.note: to savour is to taste

explanation.surface: Sampling a French dish carefully, but not as the first taster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' trims SAVOUR to AVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to try hard to achieve something.

clue.text: Commercial I appear in crops up now and then

indicators.note: the commercial and the I go inside the shuffled crops
up here means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Someone who appears in an advert that crops up occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges CROPS into SPORC; 'in' puts ADI inside it. The definition is an adverb phrase for an adjective, as in rain that falls now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic describes things occurring at irregular intervals, occasionally.

clue.text: Bishop or oarsman? One's in debt

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a rower is an oarsman

explanation.surface: A question of whether a man is a bishop or a rower, and which one owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrower owes money to the lender, so is in debt.

clue.text: Back-to-front child keeps Anglican journalist at home writing a record of what has gone on

definitions.text: a record of what has gone on

indicators.note: the shifted child holds the other pieces within
the front letter of the word moves to the back

parts.note: sprog is British slang for a child
CE is the Church of England
ed, editor, is a journalist
in means at home

explanation.surface: A child holding a church journalist at home while writing up the minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-to-front' moves the S of SPROG to the end, giving PROGS, which 'keeps' CEEDIN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceedings are the written record of a meeting or society's business.

clue.text: Waited on Georgia in the wine shop

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places one piece after another

parts.note: bode is an old past tense of bide, to wait
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone served a Georgian customer in a wine shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar.

clue.text: Hospital department pursues Neddy for approval

indicators.note: the hospital department follows behind the donkey

parts.note: Neddy is a British pet name for a donkey, an ass
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A hospital department chases a donkey to get permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent means agreement or approval.

clue.text: Thin for choice

definitions.meaning: thin, as of air at altitude

explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean thin or sparse, and also exceptionally fine or choice.

clue.text: Lent old dictator nothing, America being very discriminating

parts.note: Lent is a time of fasting, so a fast
Idi Amin was a former dictator of Uganda
O looks like zero, nothing
US is America

explanation.surface: An old dictator lent nothing to a very choosy America.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastidious means very attentive to detail and hard to please, discriminating.

clue.text: A cost to produce opera

indicators.note: producing something out of the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A remark on what it costs to stage an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's famous opera.

clue.text: A case for sewing being included in private tuition

indicators.note: included in signals the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: Private lessons in sewing come with a needle case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and sewing items.

clue.text: When there's fluff on implements, stop work

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the fluff comes before the implements

parts.note: down is soft fluffy feathers
tools are implements

explanation.surface: Workers halt when their tools get fluffy.
explanation.definitionFit: To down tools is an idiom for stopping work, as in a strike.

clue.text: 22 without point is relative

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the 22 word surrounds the point

parts.note: the answer to 22 across means nice in its old sense of fussy
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Being fussy without a point is relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice in its older sense means fastidious. 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a relative, the daughter of one's sibling.

clue.text: Bag the haulier

explanation.definitionFit: A carrier is a plastic shopping bag in British usage, and also a haulage company.

clue.text: A Turkish governor coming upon worker in a state of temporary inactivity

definitions.text: in a state of temporary inactivity

parts.note: a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A Turkish governor stumbles upon an idle worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyant means in abeyance, suspended or temporarily inactive.
